# Inessa Skorodinsky — Brand, Experience and Design Leader

> Inessa Skorodinsky is a Philadelphia-based creative and design leader with nearly three decades of experience across healthcare, financial services, and technology. She connects brand strategy and hands-on design with the teams, workflows, and standards that help organizations deliver consistent work. Her portfolio demonstrates both the creative work and the management systems behind it.

Inessa is open to Director and Senior Director opportunities in creative leadership, design leadership, brand experience, and creative operations. She also consults selectively through Teaspoon Agency.

## Leadership profile

Inessa brings experience building an in-house creative function, implementing a global brand across markets, and translating complex information into communications people can use. She works across strategy, concept development, design direction, and delivery, with particular attention to team capability and the end user's experience.

At Vanguard, she helped restructure a fragmented creative function into a full-service in-house agency. The work included a shared Creative Services mandate, centralized intake, tiered project support, clearer handoffs among Operations, Design, and Editorial, and a shared assessment of team skills. Mentorship, role development, and design goals tied to marketing objectives formed part of that operating model.

The Leadership case study reports team and organizational results including $27M in enterprise cost avoidance, 97% talent retention, a 19% efficiency gain, and a team of more than 20 people. These are results presented in the portfolio's Vanguard case study, rather than claims of individual attribution or annual recurring savings.

## Core capabilities

- Creative and design leadership: defining a creative function's purpose, directing work, developing talent, and connecting design decisions to business objectives.
- Creative operations: shared intake, prioritization, capacity visibility, project triage, briefs, cross-functional handoffs, and practical review processes.
- Brand strategy and global brand management: translating brand direction into standards, asset libraries, communications, and consistent applications across markets and formats.
- Campaign concepts and art direction: developing visual ideas around the audience and the product or service, from pencil sketches through finished executions.
- Editorial design and data storytelling: organizing complex financial and clinical information through narrative structure, typography, and visual hierarchy.
- Product and UX design: information architecture, user flows, interface planning, financial information products, and digital communications.
- Interactive learning: structuring clinical material through sequence, pacing, visual hierarchy, and activities that help users apply what they learn.
- AI-supported creative practice: a leadership perspective on using AI to assist exploration and repetitive production, while retaining human judgment, audience understanding, and responsibility for the result.

## Selected experience and work

- [Vanguard creative leadership](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/leadership.html): Operating models, creative process and triage, skills assessment, designer taxonomy, and team goals aligned with marketing objectives. The page includes the underlying management artifacts.
- [Vanguard: How America Saves](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/craft.html#editorial): Narrative structure and data visualization for an annual retirement research report. Broader Vanguard work includes institutional sales and acquisition materials, thought leadership, conference communications, and Client Center support.
- [Healthcare campaign concepts](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/craft.html#campaigns): Sketch-to-execution examples and campaigns for brands including Eliquis, Exforge, Eylea, Kapvay, and Apligraf. Pitch concepts were developed for Merck, AstraZeneca, Pfizer, and Novo Nordisk; this describes pitch work, not an assertion that every pitch became a client engagement.
- [Print format as part of the idea](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/craft.html#campaigns): The Exforge detail aid uses its physical format to carry the campaign concept. Related print-format work spans Bala Consulting Engineers, Apligraf, and PricewaterhouseCoopers.
- [Tyco International and global brand management](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/craft.html#identity): Implementation of a global rebrand across international markets, including standards, asset libraries, events, branded environments, and communications. Broader brand management experience spans Vanguard, Merck, and Bala Consulting Engineers.
- [Merck brand applications](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/craft.html#merck): Januvia and Steps to Balance materials carrying a consistent identity across websites, patient education, and print.
- [Product and UX development](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/craft.html#digital): User flows and interface planning, Dow Jones financial news products, financial data visualization, and digital newsletters. This collection includes work across organizations; not every sample is a Dow Jones project.
- [Pharmaceutical learning modules](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/craft.html#elearning): Interactive educational materials designed to make complex clinical information easier to follow and apply.

## Point of view and writing

Inessa's creative philosophy is business to human: in every assignment, she works for the person who will use the result. Business goals give the work direction; the audience's needs guide language, sequence, visual hierarchy, and interaction. Her drawing background supports an approach in which the idea comes before the tool.

- [AI and the death of creative](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/thoughts.html#ai-and-the-death-of-creative): AI as support for designers, creating more time for research, experimentation, critique, and design thinking.
- [Why creative organizations fail](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/thoughts.html#ch1): The organizational risks of depending on a few people to repeatedly rescue projects.
- [What brand governance actually means](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/thoughts.html#ch2): Giving teams usable standards, clear ownership, and room to make sound decisions.
- [Why AI changes operations more than creativity](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/thoughts.html#ch3): Evaluating AI through practical workflows, review effort, and time returned to creative work.
- [Designing teams instead of org charts](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/thoughts.html#ch4): Building around capabilities, project needs, mentorship, and growth.
- [Business-to-human communication](https://inessaskorodinsky.com/thoughts.html#ch5): Making complex information understandable without removing necessary detail.
